visualReview.notes: Inspected the combined site, four turntable directions, the buttressed square and round vats, ore loading ramp, furnace, boiler, flue, northern tanks and adobe laboratory. Reviewed the updated earth ramp and furnace pad on the original ground after the first capture revealed a terrain overlap.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the ten shared-surface and placement frames. The flat geographic fixture partly occludes the low northern group. The northern group, tanks and flue are visible in the separate original-ground and medium-fi views. Material bindings and unload passed.

mediumFiReview.notes: Inspected all 26 current frames, including the explicit four-level and transition comparisons. The square vat, four ring vats, five groups and loading ramp survive at all levels. Close views show hollow tanks, flues, cast fittings and shallow adobe wall fragments.

geographicReview.notes: The 602256 register boundary and the mapped Mount Isa rail line anchor the Cloncurry site. The unaltered independent 512 m elevation field was inspected with every group. Individual coordinates and relative level estimates are documented. The shared preview uses a flat placement fixture.

fidelityReview.scope: Present-day reconstruction of the five documented archaeological groups of Cloncurry’s Mount Elliott mill, including the crusher and ramp, roasting furnace and boiler remains, square and circular leaching vats, north electrolytic works, and adobe laboratory foundations.
fidelityReview.notes: The Queensland Heritage Register establishes the five archaeological groups, materials, relative positions and dimensions of the square vat, round vats, historic furnace and northern tanks. Exact internal outlines, flue bends, wear, spoil and fitting sizes are estimates.

imageryReview.notes: Started with the Qualla originals and linked catalogue. The historical hero's current rendition differs from the batch fingerprint, and the holding catalogue did not confirm the exact source publication. The contemporary tank photo requires attribution. The reconstruction uses official written and geographical evidence.

primaryFactsReview.notes: Queensland’s register fixes five groups and dimensions of the square vat, four round vats, northern tanks and historical furnace. State boundary, mapped railway and source terrain set the site frame. The internal positions and details are estimates.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Five visible groups of the Cloncurry Mount Elliott treatment plant and mill.

limitations: This is an exterior reconstruction of the documented archaeological remains of the Cloncurry treatment site. Equipment and the dimensions of the large vat, four round vats and three northern tanks follow the register. The present state is approximated from the documented remains and original terrain.

Individual footprints within the surveyed heritage boundary, excavation levels, surviving adobe course counts, debris, flue sections and fitting dimensions are estimates. The developed geometry reflects five surviving groups, with the roofs and full operating machinery omitted.

The published Qualla historical hero has conflicting recorded and current renditions, and the modern tank photograph requires attribution. No photograph or aerial imagery was adopted as a modeling reference.
